lem:local.detail: The displayed definition of $N_{h_0}(v)$ uses radius $h$, while its subscript and the proof's use of $h<h_0$ determine radius $h_0$. Independently, $\sigma_h^2=\operatorname{Var}(\ell_h)+E\ell_h^2$ in the instance below. The proof bounds the full kernel integral using density bounds that hold only near $v$; its reference to Lemma \ref{lemma:global} supplies a proof pattern, not additional hypotheses.
lem:local.witness: Let $v=0$, $h_0=1/8$, $W=V$, $\Gamma=\mathbb L_2$, $m(W,\gamma)=\gamma(V)$, $\gamma_0=1$, and $Y=1+\varepsilon$ for an independent Rademacher $\varepsilon$. Thus $\alpha_0=\alpha_0^{\min}=1$, $U_1=\ell_h-1$, $U_2=\varepsilon$, and every listed moment condition holds. Take $f_V$ proportional to $1_{|x|<1/4}+(1-x)^{-9/10}1_{1/2<x<1}$. Let $K$ be the normalized sum of $1_{|u|\leq1}$ and symmetric indicator pulses centered at $\pm u_n$, of half-width $e_n=u_n^{-4}$, where $u_n=2^{n^2+4}$. This kernel is bounded, symmetric, nonnegative, and has unit mass. At $h_n=1/u_n$, the pulse sampling the density singularity gives $\omega_{h_n}\gtrsim u_n^{9/10}e_n^{1/10}=u_n^{1/2}\to\infty$. Since $K^2\leq\|K\|_\infty K$, $h_n\sigma_{h_n}^2\leq2\|K\|_\infty/\omega_{h_n}\to0$, contradicting $\sigma_h\asymp h^{-1/2}$.

lem:local.suggested_repair:
corrected statement: \label{lemma:local}
Suppose $\alpha_0^{\min}$ exists and $\Gamma=\mathbb{L}_2$. Further suppose there exist $(\tilde{\alpha}, \check{\alpha}, \tilde{c}, \bar c, \tilde{f}, \bar f, \bar f', h_0)$ bounded away from zero and above such that the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Control of representer absolute value:
    $$
0< \tilde{\alpha} \leq \alpha_0(w) \leq \check{\alpha}.
$$
  \item Valid neighborhood. There exists $N_{h_0}(v)=\{v':|v'-v|\leq h_0\}\subset \mathcal{V}$.
    \item Bounded moments. For all $h\leq h_0$ and for $q=2,3,4$,
    $$
    U_1=m_h(W,\gamma_0)-E\{m_h(W,\gamma_0)\},\quad \|U_1\|_{\text{\normalfont pr},q}\leq \bar{c}\|\ell\|_{\text{\normalfont pr},q}.
    $$
    \item Bounded heteroscedasticity. For $q=2,3,4$,
    $$
    U_2=Y-\gamma_0(W),\quad \tilde{c}\leq \|U_2 \mid W\|_{\text{\normalfont pr},q}\leq \bar{c}.
    $$
    \item Bounded density. The density $f_V$ obeys, for all $v'$ in $N_{h_0}(v)$,
    $$
  0< \tilde{f} \leq f_V(v') \leq \bar f,\quad |\partial f_V(v')| \leq \bar f'.
    $$
\end{enumerate}
Suppose in addition that $\operatorname{Var}(U_2\mid W)\geq c_0>0$ almost surely; that, for $q=2,3,4$ and all sufficiently small $h$, $\int|K(u)|^qf_V(v-hu)\,du\leq C_K<\infty$ and $|\omega_h|\leq C_\omega<\infty$; and that $\inf_{0<h<h_0}|\omega_h|>0$. Suppose also that, for every $\gamma\in\mathbb{L}_2$ and all sufficiently small $h$,
$$
E\{\ell_h(V)m(W,\gamma)\}=E\{\ell_h(V)\alpha_0(W)\gamma(W)\}.
$$
Then finite sample bounds in the proof hold. In summary,
$$
\frac{\kappa_h}{\sigma_h} \lesssim h^{-1/6} \lesssim \sigma_h \asymp \bar{M}_h \asymp h^{-1/2} \rightarrow \infty,\quad \kappa_h\lesssim h^{-2/3} \rightarrow \infty,\quad \zeta_h\lesssim h^{-3/4} \rightarrow \infty.
$$ · added hypotheses: ass:patch-local-conditional-variance: $\operatorname{Var}(U_2\mid W)\geq c_0>0$ almost surely.; ass:patch-local-kernel-density: For $q=2,3,4$ and all sufficiently small $h$, $\int|K(u)|^qf_V(v-hu)\,du\leq C_K<\infty$ and $|\omega_h|\leq C_\omega<\infty$.; ass:patch-local-weighted-riesz: For every $\gamma\in\mathbb{L}_2$ and all sufficiently small $h$, $E\{\ell_h(V)m(W,\gamma)\}=E\{\ell_h(V)\alpha_0(W)\gamma(W)\}$. · gives up: patch hypothesis ass:patch-local-conditional-variance: weakens the contribution: conditioning on the pinned full vector $W$ excludes exactly identified instrumental-variable models with deterministic outcome residuals, even when the local oracle variance has the claimed rate. For example, an independent Rademacher error added to $Y$ in the model below satisfies this patch condition with $c_0=1$. A lower bound on the variance of the full oracle score would retain the excluded model.
patch hypothesis ass:patch-local-weighted-riesz: weakens the contribution: the identity excludes local functionals whose representer has the claimed rates without equaling $\ell_h\alpha_0$. For example, $m(w,\gamma)=\gamma(w)+\frac12\int_{-1}^{1}\gamma(t)\,dt$ has this property. The words allow either a bandwidth threshold common to every $\gamma$ or one depending on $\gamma$; the amended proof requires the common threshold. The condition is satisfiable: $m(w,\gamma)=\gamma(w)$ with $\alpha_0=1$ satisfies it.
